_readme: Sourcing ledger for app/public/people/*.webp, promised by docs/AVATARS.md ('The prompts are kept with each Higgsfield job and repeated in app/public/people/manifest.json once the images are brought into the repository.') but never created.

Each key is the stable person id (the filename stem before -64/-128/-256/-512). kind is 'generated' (Higgsfield, project 'CyberJudah People Avatars', workspace 28f5ce8d-ddb7-41e6-b137-a3c55b619076) or 'archival' (a real public-domain work, not generated).

status 'approved' / 'awaiting_review' is copied verbatim from docs/AVATARS.md, not re-judged here. status 'needs_confirmation' or 'documented_but_not_hosted' marks a gap this seat found but could not close without inventing data (rule 3, ops/RULES.md): see note.

This file currently covers only the ids docs/AVATARS.md documents with enough detail to record without guessing. The live app/public/people/ directory holds well over 150 further ids (ordinary avatars from Batches 2-3 onward, and the People portraits reused onto Timeline events) with no job id recorded anywhere in the repo yet. Their generation jobs do exist and are readable from the Higgsfield project's history (confirmed by this seat, 2026-10-06), but matching each live .webp to its correct job record needs a visual/hash match against that history, batch by batch -- tracked as follow-up work, not done here to avoid mis-attributing the wrong job to the wrong file.

abraham-gen-11-26.model: nano_banana_pro (requested); Higgsfield reported the jobs as nano_banana_2
abraham-gen-11-26.note: Style anchor for the pilot; used as an image reference for the rest of the set. Before Sinai, so no fringes. Approved 2026-10-01 (docs/AVATARS.md section 4).

israel-gen-25-26.note: Jacob (Israel); before Sinai. Regenerated without a face reference because using Abraham's portrait as a reference copied his face too (docs/AVATARS.md section 4, 'Review of the pilot').

esau-gen-25-25.note: Genesis 25:25. First version was a saturated sunburnt red that read as caricature; regenerated with a natural ruddy complexion, later reused as the reference complexion for Pilate, Tiberius and the Herods in batch 1.

moses-exo-2-10.note: Fringes with a ribband of blue. The pilot version had twisted, loc-like hair rather than tight woolly coils; replaced in batch 1 with tight woolly coils (docs/AVATARS.md sections 4-5).

paul-act-7-58.note: Acts 21:38; bare-headed. Regenerated without a face reference (see Israel).

david-rut-4-17.note: 1 Samuel 16:12 'ruddy' kept as a warm undertone. docs/AVATARS.md's 'Owner's verdicts on round 2' (section 9.5) lists 'the replaced David ... portraits' among what the owner approved, but no replacement job id is recorded anywhere in the repo. The file currently live may be this pilot job or an undocumented later one -- flagging rather than guessing which.

esther-est-2-7.note: Head covering. Same gap as David: the round-2 verdicts mention a replaced Esther portrait with no job id recorded.

judah-gen-29-35.note: Before Sinai. Also reused onto a Timeline event (docs/AVATARS.md section 9.5, round 3, 'People portraits reused').

solomon-2sa-5-14.note: Song of Solomon 1:5. Fringes and a ribband of blue added in round 2 (owner: 'fire').

pilate-mat-27-2.note: Edom; ruddy as Esau. Not one of the six figures later replaced with an online archival image.

tiberius-mat-22-17.note: Edom; ruddy as Esau. Not replaced.

herod-act-12-1.note: Herod Agrippa I; Edom, ruddy as Esau. docs/AVATARS.md records this as generated and kept in batch 1, but this seat did not find a herod-act-12-1 file in the current app/public/people/ listing -- flagging the discrepancy rather than guessing why.

agrippa-act-25-13.note: Agrippa II; Edom, ruddy as Esau. Same discrepancy as herod-act-12-1: documented as kept in batch 1 but not found in the current directory listing.

pharaoh-exo-1-11.note: Pharaoh of Exodus 1; Hamite, nemes. Approved in the pilot, but not found in the current directory listing, which instead has pharaoh-exo-3-10 and pharaoh-gen-37-36 (neither documented in docs/AVATARS.md at all).

Herod the Great's included' as approved. Recording both rather than silently picking one. James Tissot's 'Herod' (Brooklyn Museum) was found and explicitly rejected: it paints Herod dark-skinned, against the assembly's teaching on Edom.
